text.p: Paracelsian Inc said Monday it has canceled proposed product launches of AndroVir and AndroCar as dietary supplements following a U.S. Food and Drug Administration determination that the products are drugs, not diet supplements.

"The FDA has made it very clear that the company's plan to market AndroVir and AndroCar as dietary supplements, targeted respectively to the AIDS community and to cancer patients, would cause the FDA to classify these products as drugs, not dietary supplements," Paracelsian chairman and president Keith Rhodes said in a press release.

"Given the FDA's position, we have determined that it would not be economically viable to introduce these products as dietary supplements for the general population," he said. "Accordingly, we are canceling our dietary supplement strategies for AndroVir and AndroCar at this time."
Trading of the company's stock was halted by Nasdaq at about 1000 EDT/ 1400 GMT for the news.
The company said it is exploring other near-term options related to Andrographis paniculata and other compounds in its library.
